message.content:
The user reports that the loading spinner on the "Check" button in the storefront ZIP code checker widget looks bad - the spinner is overlapping with the "Check" text. Look at the screenshot description: the button shows a spinner circle overlapping with "Check" text inside a purple/indigo button.

Find the widget JavaScript code that handles the loading state of the Check button, and fix the spinner so it:
1. Replaces the text entirely while loading (don't show both spinner and text overlapping)
2. The spinner should be centered in the button
3. Looks clean and professional

Search for the widget code in the project - it could be in `extensions/` folder, `public/` folder, or served from an API route. Look for the button loading/spinner CSS and JS.

After fixing, run `npm run typecheck` from `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Pinzo` to verify no errors.

content.text: Let me find the widget JavaScript code first.
The widget code is in the Liquid extension files. Let me read all three block files to find the button and spinner code.

I can now see the full picture. The issue is in the `setBtnLoading` function and the related CSS. Here is exactly what is happening: - The button HTML is: `[search icon]Check` - When loading, `setBtnLoading` sets `iconEl.innerHTML = ICONS.spinner` (which is ``) and hides the label via `labelEl.style.display = 'none'` - The CSS for `.zcc-btn--loading` sets `gap:0` and `justify-content:center`, but the icon span still has the class `zcc-btn-icon` which is `inline-flex` — so the spinner renders inside a `` which is inside the button The root issue: `.zcc-btn--loading .zcc-btn-icon` has `display:flex` set, but the parent button still has `display:flex` with alignment to center — the spinner is inside an additional wrapper span, creating a double-nested flex context. The label is hidden but may still occupy space, or the spinner wrapper is misaligned. The cleanest fix: when loading, replace the entire button content with just the centered spinner, and restore it on completion. The most robust approach is to change the button to use `position:relative` and show an absolutely-centered spinner while hiding all content. Let me implement a clean fix: 1. In `setBtnLoading`, instead of toggling the icon and hiding the label, replace the full button innerHTML with just the spinner when loading, and restore the original HTML when done. 2. Update the spinner CSS to ensure it stands alone and is centered.

content.text: The code looks correct. Now run the typecheck:

Typecheck passes with zero errors. Here is a summary of what was changed and why.

---

## What was fixed

**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Pinzo/extensions/zip-code-widget/blocks/zip-code-checker.liquid`

### Root cause
The old `setBtnLoading` manipulated two separate child elements inside the button: it swapped the icon span's `innerHTML` to the spinner and hid the label span via `style.display = 'none'`. The CSS tried to compensate with `.zcc-btn--loading` overrides, but the spinner was still nested inside `.zcc-btn-icon` (an extra flex wrapper), causing it to be left-aligned or offset from center — and on some themes the label was still occupying space or flashing before hiding.

### Fix 1 — `setBtnLoading` function (lines 491–508)
The button now stores its original innerHTML on first wire-up (`btnOriginalHtml`). When loading starts, `btn.innerHTML` is replaced entirely with a single `<span class="zcc-spinner">` — no icon wrapper, no label, nothing else. When loading ends, the original markup is restored and the label text is re-synced from `cfg.buttonText`.

This eliminates any possibility of text/spinner overlap because only one element exists in the button during loading.

### Fix 2 — CSS `.zcc-btn--loading` rule (line 346)
Removed the now-unnecessary `justify-content:center` override (`.zcc-btn` already sets this on the button) and the `.zcc-btn--loading .zcc-btn-icon` flex rule (that wrapper no longer exists during loading). The `.zcc-btn--loading` rule now only sets `gap:0` as a precaution.

The spinner is automatically centered because `.zcc-btn` already declares `display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center`, so the lone `.zcc-spinner` child sits perfectly in the middle of the button.
